ety.text: Borrowed from French ballet. Further from Italian balletto, from Latin ballō + -ittus (whence Italian -etto, French -et).
Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic ваꙗтель (vajatelĭ). By surface analysis, вая́ть (vajátʹ) + -тель (-telʹ).

ety.text: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic мьгновениѥ (mĭgnovenije), from Proto-Slavic *mьgnovenьje, from *mьgnǫti (“to blink”), from *migati (“to blink”).

ety.text: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *plačь. Cognate to пла́кать (plákatʹ) and to Old Church Slavonic плачь (plačĭ).
пол- (pol-, “half”) + век (vek, “century”), with век (vek) in the genitive case. Oblique and plural cases based on полу́- (polú-, “half”).

x: Лань моя́ убега́ет.
